title: Orecchiette with Broccoli
subtitle: A Puglian pasta with broccoli, garlic, and chilli
excerpt: Small ear-shaped pasta cooked with broccoli until tender, then tossed with olive oil, garlic, chilli flakes, and pecorino. A complete supper with almost no effort.
sourceNotes: Puglian tradition; cime di rapa is classic but broccoli is the everyday substitute.

content.text: Orecchiette with broccoli is a dish from Puglia, where the pasta and vegetable cook together so the broccoli breaks down into the sauce. The key is not to drain the broccoli dry: some of that starchy water is what ties everything together.

items.prepNote: cut into small florets, stalk thinly sliced

content.text: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the orecchiette and cook for 3 minutes less than the packet time.
Add the broccoli to the same pan with the pasta. Cook together for the final 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender. Reserve a large mug of the cooking water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a frying pan over a low heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. If using anchovies, add them now. Cook gently for 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold and the anchovies have dissolved.
Drain the pasta and broccoli loosely. Tip them into the frying pan. Add 4 tablespoons of the pasta water.
Toss everything together over a medium heat for 2 minutes. Use a spoon to break some of the broccoli into the sauce. Add more pasta water if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve with pecorino over the top and a thread of olive oil.

items.cause: It was added too early and overcooked.
items.fix: Add broccoli only in the last 3 minutes of pasta cooking; it only needs to be tender, not falling apart.

items.cause: Too little pasta water was added when tossing.
items.fix: Add pasta water a splash at a time while tossing until the dish looks saucy and coated.

items.cause: The heat was too high and the garlic coloured too fast.
items.fix: Warm oil and garlic together from cold over a very low heat; it should turn pale gold in 3 to 4 minutes, not seconds.
